videos.title: How REALISTIC is Poly Bridge 2? Explained by a REAL CIVIL ENGINEER

top_comments.author: @wallacesantos0
top_comments.text:
I did some researches and posted it on reddit one time about the exact weight and maximum stress forces of the PB2 materials.

Turns out that while all the materials have no mass, and only the nodes have a mass of 0.25Pg, the roads have a mass by piece + length + node.
Each meter of the normal road is 0.25Pg.
Each piece is 0.5Pg.
Each node is 0.25Pg, like everything else.
While for the reinforced roads, the meter and the segment have a mass of 0.3125 and 0.625 Polygrams respectively.

top_comments.author: @Silent_Wings-IX
top_comments.text: Alternate title: Real engineer tries to go to space without reading instructions.

top_comments.author: @beardedterror
top_comments.text:
Hey there! I've got over 600 hours in KSP. Here are a few tips that will make your life easier:

1. Check your staging. The reason your parachute kept going off right at launch was because you had the engines and the parachute in the same stage. Add an extra stage, and they can be controlled separately!
2. Before launch, press 't'. This will turn on stability assist and (somewhat) stabilize the rocket.
3. Fins on the bottom of your rocket will make it much, much easier to control and far more stable. I'm fond of the AV-R8 winglets.
4. In the VAB, there's a circle with a dot in your control panel on the left. Click on that, and you can get automatic symmetry for your rocket.
5.. I strongly recommend starting in Science mode for your first play through. Sandbox is cool and all, but unless you've gone through the progression of the tech tree, it's tough to know which pieces to use and when.

top_comments.author: @mtbrocket
top_comments.text: This isn’t a road game, it is a development control game. Don’t block all development, just guide it. I think you should place roundabouts as soon as you get them. They do nothing while in storage and don’t help with emergency fixes due to their size requirements. Put them down as soon as you get them at potential choke points and they block development. Also run parallel roads next to each other instead of one apart so houses can’t spawn between. Make fake roundabouts using 3x3 road squares so once you get roundabouts they can fill in these spots. In the beginning congestion is ok from odd road configurations if it reduces congestion latter in the game by making it easier to build. I would call these future corridors using road bits. Road bits do nothing while in storage. So lay them out. Tear them up only when required to. Don’t hook up every house but do keep escape passages clear using road bits. Running roads along the side of rivers early on helps block development that can block bridges. And as you know, the more bridges the better! :-)

I have a humble suggestion. Absolutely love the lawn mowing series. However, it is difficult to follow the series without going through your "videos" tab. Even though it is a 3 part series, your videos are not recommended in a sequential manner due to a lack of numbering. If you could add something such as "Part 1, 2 3" or "#1, #2, #3" in your titles, it will not only be a comfort for viewers to follow the series, but it will also promote the YouTube algorithm to push your series more.

- YouTube Gaming Channels often number their series, even if they do 3 or 4 videos on one game.

- YouTube wants to achieve maximum viewership from one viewer, which can be achieved effectively with the help of a series, just like Lawn Mowing Simulator.

top_comments.author: @tomasball6642
top_comments.text: Just a little tip in regards to food and water. When playing I've found the best way to stay on top of food is to have say 2 - 4 farm houses per farm you have and build heaps of storage because the hold up with farming isn't really actually how much the crops grow its how much is harvested, stored and planted. So if you have lots of people harvesting and lots of storage you'll have a heap of food and never run out. A prime example is your wheat farm, those crop circles are basically because the wheat is growing too fast for the beavers to harvest enough. And with water, the more storage the more water you'll accumulate over time.

top_comments.author: @Madnessnunky
top_comments.text: From what I recall reading about this game, demand increases linearly over time, so single color shops get harder and harder to satisfy when they are the ONLY one on the map. If you did this same strategy but opened up space for new shops in specific places, the overall demand would get spread out and you need fewer cars per location to keep the timers down. Green may need 10 cars per second, but split over three shops would mean some 2-3 houses per could keep up no problem.

Just a few pointers I would like to give:

top_comments.text: Airplane knowledge: The flappy things on the ends of airplane wings are the ailerons, and they're used to bank (Also known as turning). top_comments.author: @SeatedOvation
top_comments.text: RCE! You appear to be confused on the district limits settings. Each district has its own limits, high and low. A districts LOW limit is the minimum amount to keep in that district when deciding to ship items out. A districts high limit is the maximum amount to bring into the district when deciding to ship items in. Therefore a trade route between two districts concerns the outgoings low setting and the incomings high settings. The opposite settings will have no effect, unless opposite trade routes were established going the other way or to other districts. For example: to send some, but not all water to Shameville from Beaverville, Beaverville should have a minimum value of 500(or so) and shameville should have a maximum of 70. That would ensure that Beaverville never goes below 500, regardless of where its sending it to, and Shameville would never go above 70, regardless of where its coming from. Hopefully this helps you and your fellow engineers in your future beaver escapades!

top_comments.author: @Zwamdurkel
top_comments.text:
Many tips please read:

The poison sprayers are doing something. They are OP against shields and do damage in their whole "spray". 
!!! you want to make sure to place them somewhere they can fire in a straight line to maximize their effectiveness. (flame tower too) !!!
The reason you don't see the poison icon is because the 80 poison/sec is too fast.

Oogie spawns on the longest path, as long as that isn't the path you most recently expanded.

You usually want to destroy shields first, then armor, then health

A good tactic is to make a kill zone where all paths gather to make the towers most useful.

Universities are OP. Try to start using them around lvl 25

Lookout tower is also insane: it adds the multipliers to all towers attacking the target. Since total damage is calculated using multiplication... yeah you get it.

Be sure to upgrade the towers near your tower manually since they can't really level by themselves.

top_comments.author: @Sandman4700
top_comments.text: You choose so many different tower cards instead of upgrading like 5 towers to be beast. Its 44 cards total, so if you choose 9 towers , your left with 35 cards and an average of 4 upgrades per tower. The pool of upgrades increases when a new tower is picked. This opens you up to tons of tower upgrade options, which limits your actual choices every round when your trying for specific cards. Essentially you have so many cards available, you are less likley to get the upgrade your seeking as there are so many other options it can display. If you choose 5 towers, your left with 39 cards. This is an average of 8 upgrades per tower, and doesnt muddy the card pool for upgraging what you want. This allows you to achieve helpful options that make towers more effective, instead of just more different towers that throw cotton balls.

top_comments.author: @DuckInGameStop
top_comments.text: You should check the difficulty settings of your world, if you're on a harder one your stuff will just disappear instead of being stored in a container when you die. Also, there's a bug where the containers can spawn way underground and you need to edit its position in the world file to make your stuff reachable again. (Someone made a very helpful Steam Guide on how to do this) One time I died and never found the stuff I dropped, but once I read that Guide I was able to find the container in the world file and it was at y = -147! I changed the y coordinate to 20 and I was able to recover all my stuff, you should try it too! (Make a backup of the world first though, by copying and pasting it, just in case you do it wrong and it gets corrupted)

top_comments.text: I use a technique starting mid-game that allows me to finish a whole lvl 7/8 ship in 1 shift. There is essentially 3 layers to every ship, the hull which goes to the processor, the frame that goes into the furnace and the interior (some exterior) components that are loaded onto the barge. What I realized is that the frame (all furnace pieces) only make up 1-2% of the entire ship so... I rip off the hull and then use strong tethers to pull the frame with all interior components to the barge giving me a grade 5. I lose 1-2% for the frame but saves hours of meticulously pulling everything out and launching it to the barge. Happy shipbreaking!

I think you are a little bit off with your velocity assumption:
In a closed pipe a reduction of the diameter results in a higher velocity (with an incompressible fluid). But because your system is open, the fluid uses the open space above to release the "pressure" of the reduced diameter and just stacks higher (as you noticed). So the physics are probably correct :)

Edit: In a continous stream you should be correct, there the velocity should be higher in a narrower channel, but I think the tidal wave breaks the system because it generates a local pressure at the entrance of the narrow channel.

top_comments.author: @Ravenishish
top_comments.text: Ah, Mr Engineer. So this is a common programming issue where you can have super-efficient programs or super small programs but in a lot of cases you can't do both (usually you're aiming somewhere in the middle depending on computing power/data throughput/other active concurrent threads...it's a whole thing). The way to speed up this one is turn the conveyor belts into readers pointing the colour you're ignoring at each other and instead of throwing them back onto the middle track when they're empty dump them in the fire pits directly (that eliminates yet another check) gives you a bulky thing but it will run so much faster. (Heck, even having two readers pointing at each other instead of a second conveyor belt will pretty much halve your time without adding all the fire pits but will break your lower size limit because you need to feed the blues into success pits so you might as well bloat the thing if you're going for max speed)

top_comments.author: @OG_Casual_Tryhard
top_comments.text:
Hey RCE, just wanted you to know that your framerate loss isn't from the "amount" of resources in your bridges. It's about 90% because of the shard bars in the one bridge. Hydroneers lighting/shadows/reflections optimization isn't all that great, and EACH ONE of those bars is a light producer, that constantly changes values. In turn creating shadows, and reflecting off of the other bars as well.
If you want to fix this fps problem, I recommend the removal of just the shard bars in particular.
We don't need a mod for your bridges, we need a lighting quality slider.
Hope you're doin well.

top_comments.text:
The final island is size 6x5, with the 4 corners missing, for a total of 26 squares.
Given that you can combine into a higher tier with 3 buildings, and the third building can be completed via the combination of three lower-tier buildings at the same time, that means we'd only need 2 buildings of each tier plus the third building of the lowest tier (let's assume tier 1 for now). We can generalize this as Spaces for Tier x = ((x-1)*2)+1. 
Utilizing this formula, we can see that we start exceeding the number of squares available only if we try to achieve a Tier 14 building or higher, meaning that, at least theoretically, you should be able to reach a Tier 13 building. You'll even have a free square available for re-organizing buildings around with the Move command, as long as you can afford it!

But we can in fact reach EVEN HIGHER tiers, if the tiers we start with are higher tiers! If we were to treat Tier 6 buildings as our most base building block (Since those are the highest tier you can buy), we'd be able to reach another 6 tiers higher for the final building, meaning we should be theoretically able to reach a tier 19(!!!) building at the max. I sure wonder if they made a model

1. Flaps on the wings of planes are extremely useful for landing and taking off. They effectively change thrust into lift. This makes it easier to land while also decelerating your plane.

top_comments.author: @Trevor21230
top_comments.text:
Tips & Tricks: 

1)don't go for the headshot upgrade with the piercing weapon; the multiplier only applies to the head segment, so most of your damage is unaffected.

2) It's very tempting to just buy the same snakes over and over.  Resist this temptation until you've actually seen all the snakes, because some are better than others for a given build.  Tiger Snakes are great for the piercing weapon, for example.

3) Of there aren't any upgrades you *really* want, just save your teeth.  The final weapon upgrades are insanely powerful and you really, really want to be able to afford them by day 9 at least.

4) Depending on the situation, getting wrapped up by a snake can actually be a very good thing.  Like if the last snake is a loot snake (lots of health, not very dangerous), getting wrapped up is completely safe and will help you kill it with fertilizer (damaging aura).

Amusing to see RCE's habit of high-prioritizing everything turn into his downfall.  When you ran out of food and water, you should have pause, de-prioritized _everything_ (including rebuilding the gigadam, which you don't need for 8 beavers) and prioritized only jobs that immediately give you food or water (carrots, berries and pumpers).

top_comments.author: @joeloreilly2953
top_comments.text: Train facts: Engineers try to keep the slope under 1%, but anything under 2.2% slope is generally accepted.  Anything more than that and it's no longer economically viable for the train line.  Greater slopes have been made, upwards of 25%, but those are designed to use the train momentum to continue up and over the hill (collecting momentum down one side of the hill and keep going up the other).  Trains can climb, it just costs a lot in fuel and efficiency.

I've been playing this game for years now. By far one of my favorite games out there and I'm glad you've found it!
Not sure if you like tips or if you have already discovered this stuff (I haven't finished the video yet), but here's what I've got:
1. Don't upgrade walls at night! It takes down the wall temporarily and lets the greedlings through!
2. Many upgrades will require you to explore other islands. It's best to speed through the first island's boat and get to the second island ASAP.
3. Destroying trees next to the merchant or vagrant camps removes the buildings. Vagrant camps can be rebuilt but hiring from rebuilt camps is expensive.
4. Give extra gold to the banker (the guy with the fancy hat)! The bank will keep excess gold safe and apply interest over time.
5. Upgraded farms will let farmers stay overnight. Excellent for farms far from your keep, but will get the farmer's tools and gold stolen by greed if the farm is outside of your walls.

REALLY IMPORTANT POINT MATT: The monthly budget DOES NOT show income from trade surplus. Only services like water and electricity are shown in the budget. Private trade surplus income is not shown as income in Cities Skylines 2. Your 263t/month oil surplus is making huge stacks, you just can't see it on the graph.

Hey Matt, some advice:
- They're sharks, not Whales [or Wales - said by a Welshman]
- You need some speed [and steering] towards the end, hence why you got caught up in that cluster ffyc

top_comments.text:
Some strategy to be aware in general:
1. unlocking a new country that is not the goal will NOT increase your time limit, so that's pretty useless
2. unlocking a new country will increase your cost to open a new route, so you should have your network substantially established (when financially viable) before unlocking
3. only routes connecting capitals can activate the supersonic plane event, but supersonic plane is only useful when the connecting capitals are some distance apart
4. passengers only take the cheapest route to their destination and doesn't care about how crowded are the airports/routes in their way
5. each route can hold at most 5 airplanes, so you should minimize your transatlantic distance. Even with 5 lv 6 plane from London to DC, they will be all full. Thus, you need multiple entry points into the US/Canada (and you must use Greenland). Also, enter South America through Africa (you don't want to overload this already stressed part of the network), which also means the connection from North to South America should be very nondirect to discourage European passengers to go up then go down

top_comments.author: @_tanoshi
top_comments.text:
Some tips I found to be very useful and that I'd loved to have known myself in the beginning.
- there is a global grid, hold ctrl when placing foundations and it'll snap to the a global grid
- when manually crafting you can just press space bar once and so you don't need to hold it
- when building conveyers, you can switch build modes with R: For conveyers you now have a "straight" more for example, or for foundations there is the zoop or vertical mode.
- middle mouse button can "select" a whatever building you are looking at
- with ctrl + c when you are close to a factory you can copy it's configuration, and with ctrl + v you can paste it to others, this works for recepies and overclocking, as well as later on for smart splitters etc.
- one of the most fun ways to travel for me (until you unlock hypertubes) are ziplines, you can unlock those in the carterium tree in the mam, tho it takes some getting use to

I could go on and on, but I guess you'll figure out most stuff on your own sooner or later. Loved the first series and can't wait to see this one :)

top_comments.author: @EtheE
top_comments.text:
Gatherers, foresters and lumberjacks calculate range by treating diagonals as equivalent to one block in either direction. This is what gives them the square ranges, and means their pathing is more efficient if they can take diagonal shortcuts to their targets instead of having to move up/down and then left/right separately.

 You blocked off the diagonal route to the birches with the industrial pile, which reduced their max range since they can't diagonally travel to the birch area anymore.

top_comments.text:
So the issues with your sluices are relatively simple to fix.

A sluice is like a controller, checking how deep the downstream is and opening/closing, depending on the downstream depth, regardless of upstream water levels. Now the issue on your first dam is, that several sluices still have some earth in front of them. They measure the water height on the block in front of them. So because of that extra dirt, they will never close. The water keeps flowing off, triggering their automatic opening mechanism. Dynamite all the dirt blocks downstream from the sluices and make sure everything is on the same level. Then you can set the downstream height to 0.8 and your farms should always be watered automatically.

Always place sluices at the bottom of your dam. That way you can ensure your dam fills up, while keeping the downstream nice and irrigated.

A sluice also checks upstream contamination. Anything up to let's say 20% contamination may look dodgy, but won't harm your farms or beavers. You can set some sluices to close above 20% contamination. These will provide the normal water for your farms and pumps. If you upgrade your fix it tool, you can make much more money because you’ll be able to upgrade everything to perfect condition, giving you the maximum possible profit. top_comments.author: @richardlanglois172
top_comments.text:
I cannot understand why you're mucking about with floodgates at your main reservoir to your secondary farm reservoir. That place is EXACTLY what sluices are for...

Put the sluices at the bottom (all the way across, the whole 6 wide). Put the floodgates (2 high) ontop of them and set their height to 1.9. Point the arrow on the floodgate _out_ of the main reservoir; the arrow points to the DOWNSTREAM direction, the direction that the water will be allowed out to. Set the sluices' height limit to 0.6. The dams further downstream will allow overflow out at 0.65.

This setup is fully automated. It will keep your farm reservoir full without wasting water, until the main reservoir is overflowing, which will pour into the farm reservoir, and overflow out the dams. You'll never need to touch it again.

top_comments.text:
When I was in high school, I opened the piano in the band room, and inside I found a treasure map!  It had a floor plan of the band room, and it showed a big X (as treasure maps are wont to do), so of course I paced it all out as directed, following the dotted lines past the bass amp, around the drums, under the bells, to the room with the music stands, across to the fire bell, and finally into the instrument room.  I moved an old saxophone case, and there was a tile with a big X on it.  Under the tile... a hollowed out spot with a tiny treasure chest!  The chest contained some satchels of candy, a few Mexican coins, and a luchador keychain trinket.

It was my favourite day of high school.  The next day I filled the box with Jolly Ranchers, a rubber beholder toy, and six ambiguously dirty poems on squares of fancy paper, and returned it to its place.  The map was stashed under the matting of an easel in the drafting room.  I graduated before anyone found it, but one of my brother's friends found it the next year.  I like to believe that decades later that old treasure map is still being passed around, and goodies are being exchanged between anonymous students via that little box.

top_comments.text:
A few thoughts on the season: 
1) One big problem you keep running into is building things that require you to intervene on time - water pumpers, floodgates, etc. That's unavoidable in the early game, but you can use things like setting the maximum depth on pumps and sluices (if you ever figure out how to use them) to automate a lot of that, which would let you focus more on your megaprojects and food. 
2) If you keep adding jobs, you either need to be turning them on and off manually or adding beavers. You can build job buffers - haulers or builders set to lowest priority, so any spare beavers do productive work - but at some point you do need to balance job additions with more beavers. 
3) You always end a season an episode or two early. I imagine you're getting bored or there's less engagement material in there if you aren't causing incidents, but it also means you skip out on using some of the cool new stuff, like tunnels, and other late game stuff like bots. Building actual underground irrigation systems would be neat and I'm sure you can figure out a way to screw it up in an entertaining way if you try.

top_comments.author: @navad108
top_comments.text: Three things: First, you have a large inventory that's accessible from the oil drums right next to the repair machines - a good place to put all the car parts since that inventory is accessible to the body shop. The second is that selling cars with better parts greatly increases your reputation gained - though getting the body shop update and an employee to do the work makes it less tedious. The third is that the junk cars on the map are visible from the minimap in the HUD only. Those are free fixer uppers and now that you have employees to get the rust off and clean them you can turn them around quickly for a good profit. Keep in mind that almost all the parts will need replacing.

top_comments.author: @Godlyhell
top_comments.text:
Excuse me, but as a Mechanical Bridge Engineer (self-titled), I must protest this 0.00/10.
This humble cue bridge is absolutely an engineered structure. Observe:
Load-bearing design: It supports the cue under torsional and lateral stress during off-center shots.
Multi-angle head geometry: Those grooves aren't decoration; theyre precision-engineered shot vectors.
Material science: Usually brass or high-impact polymer, chosen for minimal deflection under load (and to survive pool-hall rage).
Modular assembly: Detachable head, telescopic handle… that's field-adjustable engineering, my friend.
By all accounts, this is a certified piece of civil-mechanical marvel.
I’m afraid the proper rating should be at least 8.7/10. Loses points only for lacking guard rails.

Ok couple tips for you. Matt.  You were not broke throughout this episode.  You had 20 silver right next to your copper, each silver is 1000 copper.  Also you need to start paying attention to your ratios or this game will eat you alive. You had a glass kiln with one grinder feeding it?  Thats crazy, you were feeding it 5/m sand when it wanted 90/m sand.

Also, you want to sell everything you can in the shop.  Everything you unlock will be requested, by customers but i also think any teir you finish the customers will request all the lower teirs.  You need to unlock everything in the lower teirs instead of just blindly pushing straight to finish the teir.

Finally automate more.  The cash register has outputs.  Belt out your cash into storage.  Use banks to convert between different coins.   Belt your money into purchasing portals so they can buy your wood and limestone.   Then you have a fully automated shop both the buying and selling.

0:50 American here - Water compresses very poorly (and is obviously much denser than air) and thus is hard to penetrate at high velocities, which is why a bellyflop hurts or a long fall into water is deadly.  Bullets will lose all their momentum in the first foot or two, so they'd be no good unless the fish are right at the surface.  If they are near the surface tho, then a bullet doesn't even need to directly hit them - the shockwave of the bullet impacting the water can be enough to kill (but the lethality falls off exponentially with distance, thus still no good for deeper fish).

That's why in reality we Americans use dynamite to fish - bigger shockwave that can originate below the surface closer to the fish.

A tip for all you earth repopulating beavers;
The longer they stay in medical beds the faster they heal. Seems obvious right?
Thing most don't realize is that they still need food, water, and enrichment. So unless your 'hospital' is close to those things, they will leave the bed and travel all the way to where they are making their healing time longer. And they lose decor bonuses if those aren't covering the beds either.
In a large colony you wont notice this as much, but in smaller colonies where every bit of the workforce counts, or districts heavy in industries with high injury risk, it can cause an Incident out of nowhere.

top_comments.text: Your memory is correct, light as a form of energy can exert mechanical force upon an object. The amount of energy is tiny though, even for high power lasers. The De-Brogli Equation covers the momentum energy of a photon, and is the basis for the workings of solar sails.

top_comments.author: @tuseroni6085
top_comments.text:
yeah, basically all the energy of a photon is from its momentum, to show why look at expanded form of the famous e=mc^2:
e^2=(mc^2)^2+(PC)^2

when m=0, as it does in photons, MC^2=0, e^=2(PC)^2, e=PC

for a photon P=HF/C and so e=HFC/C, e=HF

the momentum is the important part, when a photon hits an object it transfers that momentum into it, if it reflects it transfers twice as much, so you want a very reflective surface.

because momentum is the frequency of the photon * a very small constant (H/C) it is a very small amount of momentum transferred. however lasers also put out a LOT of photons.

Maths/Letter code puzzle: The trick is that each letter maps onto a unique single digit number. So B*B*B=F implies B=2, F=8 because 1 and 2 are the only numbers that when cubed are a single digit, and B is not equal to F implies B cannot be 1. With that, you can work out that A must be 3, because 1, 2 and 3 are the only numbers that when squared are single digit, and 1 and 2 are not possible. And then the rest solves easily. So only one solution.
